name: wiki-manager
description: Maintain a standing LLM knowledge base compiled from a NotePlan vault, shaped as an FAQ dependency graph and partitioned into domain SPACES (family, current/former employer, business, venture, plus a public floor) each bound to a confidentiality/PII tolerance. Each article answers one question and carries a space; derived answers build on other answers, and following the links crawls down to base facts grounded verbatim in raw notes — but only within the answer's own space or the public floor, so the crawl never leaks one domain's confidential content into another (a Bell-LaPadula-style compartment model). Ingests an immutable Unorganized/raw inbox into grounded, cross-linked articles under Notes/📚 Wiki/<space>/, keeps a hub + per-space indexes + a shared append-only log, answers questions with citations per space, and lints for source fidelity, gaps, dependency cycles, broken links, cross-space compartment leaks, and space/folder mismatches. Reorganizes the inbox without rewording source content, verified by a git-backed content-preservation linter that proves no original source line is lost or reworded across a reorganization or split. No secret ever enters any space. Keeps pages lean for a first-time reader: cross-links live in frontmatter (prerequisites down, leads_to back up) rather than in body sections, so a page body is only the answer, and a running newcomer verdict per page records what to read, what to skip, and whether the page is lean or bloated — kept fresh by a content hash, so editing a page makes its verdict stale by construction. Ships a report-only SessionStart hook that surfaces what is ready to ingest, plus advisory Stop hooks for stale concept maps and stale verdicts. Because NotePlan is an editor rather than a preview — it prints formatting markers, shows HTML comments, has no callout syntax, never loads a remote image, and turns wrapped inline markup into literal text — reviews carry those limits as knowledge and read the raw markdown, reserving the capture tool (which opens an article in the app at a computed character offset past the properties panel, crops to the editor column and screenshots it) for checking how a new markdown technique or a freshly attached diagram actually lands. What a source read alone would miss is caught mechanically instead, by a render-safety check run over every page and every verdict, because a page can be hash-fresh, validator-clean and structurally broken at the same time. A review that finds an answer with a shape can also attach a PlantUML diagram to the article, rendered on the private server and downloaded as a local image with its source saved beside the PNG rather than dumped into the body.
